key_insight: Scientific machine learning can replace expensive coupled flow-and-transport simulations with fast surrogates while preserving key physics.
engineering_relevance: The methods target practical fluid-mechanics problems where high-fidelity Navier–Stokes and scalar-transport solvers are too costly for design, analysis, or repeated evaluation.
method: SVD-based reduced-order models, including Dynamic Mode Decomposition, for linear compression of flow dynamics.
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for surrogate modeling of turbidity currents.
β-Variational Autoencoders (β-VAEs) to learn disentangled nonlinear modes in thermal convection.
evidence_signal: The chapter evaluates methods on representative benchmarks such as lock-exchange flows and Rayleigh-Bénard convection, alongside turbidity-current and thermal-flow case studies.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the specific problem and data regime, so real-time prediction and uncertainty quantification are not guaranteed.
paper_title: Advances in Scientific Machine Learning for Coupled Fluid Flow and Transport
